오후 세 시에 팀 회의가 있어요.
There's a team meeting at three p.m.
I prepared coffee before the meeting.
We'll have lunch after the meeting.
후에 (hue) = after: 회의 후에 (hoeui hue = after the meeting).
I took notes in the meeting.
I'm sending the report by Friday.
생겼어요 (saenggyeosseoyo) = came up/appeared — new things happening.
정리해요 (jeongnihaeyo) = tidy up/organize — desks, files, rooms.
We start the project next month.
마감 (magam) = deadline — you'll hear it constantly in Korean offices.
We have a company dinner tonight.
회식 (hoesik) = after-work team dinner — a big part of Korean office life.
We ate pork belly at the company dinner.
삼겹살 (samgyeopsal) = grilled pork belly — the classic team-dinner menu.
The company is paying for dinner.
내요 (naeyo) = pays: 회사가 내요 = the company pays.
After the dinner we went to karaoke.
노래방 (noraebang) = karaoke room — round two of many team dinners.
늦게 (neutge) = late (adverb): 늦게 끝났어요 = ended late.
What are you going to eat for lunch?
I ate kimchi stew with my colleagues.
김치찌개 (kimchijjigae) = kimchi stew — a lunch-menu regular.
제가 사요 (jega sayo) = 'I'm buying' — how you offer to treat.
A junior colleague bought the coffee.
후배 (hubae) = your junior at work or school; your senior = 선배 (seonbae).
식사 후에 다 같이 카페에 가요.
After the meal we all go to a cafe.
On Fridays we have chicken and beer.
치맥 (chimaek) = 치킨 + 맥주, Korea's beloved chicken-and-beer combo.
The day after a company dinner I'm always tired.
When is the next company dinner?
We had birthday cake at the office.
야근 (yageun) = working overtime into the night — common office Korean.
Yesterday I worked overtime until ten.
이번 주에 야근을 세 번 했어요.
I worked late three times this week.
번 (beon) counts times, with native numbers: 세 번 (se beon = three times).
After overtime I went home by taxi.
It's hard because there's so much work.
-아서/어서 = because: 많아서 (manaseo = because there's a lot).
I'm busy every day these days.
Last week I was really busy.
별로 (byeollo) + negative = not really: 별로 없어요 = not much.
I leave work right at six.
퇴근해요 (toegeunhaeyo) = leave work — the opposite of 출근 (chulgeun).
일찍 (iljjik) = early: 일찍 퇴근했어요 = left work early.
A colleague is still at the office.
이번 달 (ibeon dal) = this month; 이번 (ibeon) = this (time).
What will you do with your salary?
My salary went up a little.
올랐어요 (ollasseoyo) = went up — salaries, prices, temperatures.
I'm looking for a new job these days.
From next month I'll be at a new company.
On weekdays I get up at six thirty.
In the morning I shower and get dressed.
-고 (go) links actions in order: 샤워하고 (syawohago = shower and then).
I usually eat breakfast at home.
I drink two cups of coffee a day.
하루에 (harue) = per day: 하루에 두 잔 = two cups a day.
Yesterday morning I got up late.
못 (mot) = can't/couldn't manage: 못 먹었어요 = couldn't eat.
Tomorrow I'll get up at six.
After lunch I take a short walk.
잠깐 (jamkkan) = for a moment: 잠깐 산책해요 = take a short walk.
I get home at seven in the evening.
In the evening I eat with my family.
At night I watch Korean dramas.
I usually go to bed at eleven.
수고했어요 (sugohaesseoyo) = 'you worked hard' — the everyday office goodbye.
I'm off first. See you tomorrow!
저 먼저 가요 (jeo meonjeo gayo) — the polite 'I'm leaving first' at the office.
On Wednesday I go to Busan on a business trip.
출장 (chuljang) = business trip: 출장을 가요 = go on a business trip.
I came back from the business trip yesterday.
다음 주 금요일에 휴가를 쓸 거예요.
I'll use a vacation day next Friday.
휴가를 써요 (hyugareul sseoyo) = 'use' vacation days — 쓰다 means write AND use.
